claims.text: Adding approximately 1–3 atomic percent boron to a phosphorus-containing CrMnFeCoNiP high-entropy alloy will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding approximately 1–3 atomic percent boron will improve the thermal stability of the alloy's amorphous state.
The baseline boron-free CrMnFeCoNiP alloy can be rapidly quenched from the melt into an amorphous structure.
Boron addition will promote the formation of boron–phosphorus bonds in the liquid and amorphous alloy.
Boron addition will promote the formation of boron–metal bonds in the liquid and amorphous alloy.
The boron-associated bonds will enhance local network connectivity.
Boron will act as a network former and increase the viscosity of the melt.
Boron will retard atomic diffusion in the alloy.
Increased viscosity and reduced atomic diffusion will hinder the nucleation and growth of crystalline phases during quenching.
Suppression of crystallization will expand the alloy's glass-forming region and increase its thermal stability.
The boron-modified alloy will have a greater critical casting thickness than the boron-free baseline.
The boron-modified alloy will have a crystallization onset temperature approximately 50–100 °C higher than the boron-free baseline.
The beneficial effect is expected only near 1–3 atomic percent boron and under rapid-quenching conditions.
Excessive boron or deviations from the specified processing conditions may cause elemental segregation or unwanted secondary-phase formation.
Boron is a well-known network former in similar amorphous systems.
